_README: Baseline for every later phase. Recomputed from the logs by baseline_snapshot.py; `python baseline_snapshot.py --check` fails if the logs no longer produce these numbers. Read `pools` before quoting any figure -- rank movement is bounded by population size and the pooled number belongs to whatever mix of runs the pool holds.

pools.all: every steps.jsonl with >= 10 scored steps, any configuration
pools.production_config: alpha=0.85, n=8, rank scorer, no baseline scorer -- the configuration PRECHECKS was measured under

pooled_ties.coverage_note: `surprise` is absent from every run that predates the flag; a tie-on-surprise figure covering 0 runs is reported as null, not as 0.

weak_half_tied_on_surprise.source: all (production pool does not log it)

vs_prechecks_note: Differences are reported, not reconciled. PRECHECKS computed these over a run set it did not record, and tuning this script until the numbers match would be fitting the measurement to the claim. What matters downstream is that a later phase compares against THIS file, recomputed the same way.

vacuity_screen.definition: heavy (mean weight > 0.14), long-lived (>= 8 steps), top-ranked (mean rank <= n/2) and a split candidate on <= 10% of its steps
